_comment: Tier 0 only. Magpie drives real benchmarks and kernel builds on GPU
hardware, so no case grades behavior yet; add one with `should` /
`should_not` plus an evals/machine.yml when a runner is available.
The near misses matter more than usual here: this skill and
tracelens-analysis-orchestrator both mention TraceLens and trace analysis,
so the boundary between 'benchmark and optimize kernels' and 'orchestrate
a trace analysis report' is the thing most likely to route wrong.

cases.prompt: Benchmark vLLM throughput and time-to-first-token for Llama 3 on this box, and capture torch traces while it runs.
I have two HIP implementations of a softmax kernel. Which one is faster, and is the optimized one still numerically correct?
Find the top bottleneck kernels in my inference workload and map the profiler names back to the source that generates them.
Rank these three Triton attention kernel variants against each other and validate the winner end to end.

cases.note: Kernel authoring, not kernel evaluation. Shares all the vocabulary and none of the workflow.
cases.prompt: Write a CUDA kernel that transposes a matrix, and explain the shared-memory tiling.
What is the theoretical peak FP16 throughput of an MI300X on paper?

cases.note: Near miss the other way: this is the analysis orchestrator's job even though Magpie also post-processes traces.
cases.prompt: Run the agentic analysis workflow on this PyTorch profiler trace and write me a prioritized analysis.md.
